First session back after two full rest days for the lower back strain, which was still present in the morning. Cable row was cut deliberately and pullups went to three sets to carry the pulling volume; the lat pulldown was kept because no chest-supported row was free. Two substitutions were forced by equipment rather than chosen: standing curls for preacher curls, and standing 15 lb Y raises for seated 20s. Both put the low back to work stabilising, which is the opposite of the intent -- worth watching against tomorrow's morning check-in. No sled, by plan, since it is tomorrow's session.

Sled only, by choice, on the fourth day after the lower-back strain and the first morning the back felt normal. Logged as "conditioning" because no program day is sled-only -- the sled is a 5-10 minute warmup or an optional finisher inside the four lifting days, never the session itself, so this will show as a deviation and should. Tiring and a heavy sweat despite no lifting, which is what fifty minutes at full resistance buys. The next lower session is being held back to Wednesday or Thursday rather than taken tomorrow.

A single full-body session by choice -- the only day this week training was possible -- covering the sled, jumps, trap bar, bench, pullups, squat and dips in one go. Typed "full-body", a session type added the same evening for this session: it had been logged as "other" for a few hours first, which was true and said nothing. No program day is full-body, so it still draws no plan comparison and still reads as the deviation it is -- the type names which deviation it was, the way "conditioning" does for a sled-only day. Performed order put pullups before the squat rather than after, which is the one departure from the plan that was not forced. The day's result is the trap bar: 240 for two sets of five, reported quite easy, eight days after the August 5 session that the lower-back strain followed, and with nothing from the back this time. That weight was first logged as 260 and corrected on August 14 -- 240 is the load the plan prescribed for re-entry, so the session complied here instead of exceeding the plan, and the day's headline is a clean back rather than a held top set. Nothing on the 13th tested 260. Bench was 150 rather than 155 only because the plates were not there. Pullups were reported quite hard, which is what taking them fifth in a full-body session five days after the last lifting day buys, and is not a reading on the path to ten. Upper traps flagged: reported as working hard on the trap bar, and reported as recurring.

THIS IS THE AWAY_FROM_THE_GYM ROUTINE, NOT THE STRETCH DAY IN PROGRAM.TS -- the no-equipment version done on day two of the August 14-19 trip, all seven daily items at the prescribed doses (the dips slot has no movement of its own; the deep pushup hold covers it). Fifteen minutes by report, against the routine's stated twelve. It is typed `stretch` at the owner's explicit choice on August 15, and that is a deliberate departure from a documented decision: the comment above AWAY_FROM_THE_GYM says the trip routine is deliberately NOT a SessionType and that days away are recorded by a breaks.csv row, precisely so that a maintenance week is not graded. The cost of overriding that is specific and should be read for what it is -- comparePlan() now grades this against the bell version of the stretch day, so the goblet pry, the kettlebell pullover, the long lunge hold and the prying floor press will show as missed slots. THEY WERE NOT SKIPPED; there were no bells and no gym, and the away routine substitutes for them on purpose (doorway squat hold for the goblet pry, bodyweight RDL with a reach for the 35 lb one, active hang for the pullover). Read every gap on this session's plan comparison as equipment, not as compliance. The alternative on the table was a new `away` session type that would draw no comparison at all; if these false gaps become annoying across the remaining trip days, that is the fix rather than editing the program. Fatigue and sweat were not reported and are left blank. OF THE THREE-ITEM FOOT BLOCK, ONLY THE SUPINATED CALF RAISE WAS DONE -- it carries no rows of its own because the routine folds it into the single-leg calf raises as an outside-edge bias, so it lives in that exercise's note. Short foot and single-leg barefoot balance were not done.
